episode_title: SQE1 And SQE2 Explained: Everything I Wish I Knew Before!
question: What are the two parts of SQE1 and what legal knowledge do they test?
transcript_excerpt: SQE1 consists of two sets of 180 multiple choice questions called FLK1 and FLK2 (Functioning Legal Knowledge). FLK1 covers business law and practice, dispute resolution, contract law, tort law, legal system of England and Wales, constitutional and administrative and EU law, and legal services. FLK2 covers property practice, wills and administration of estates, solicitors accounts, land law, trusts and criminal law and practice, with professional conduct tested on both exams.

episode_title: SQE1 And SQE2 Explained: Everything I Wish I Knew Before!
question: How is SQE2 structured differently from SQE1 in terms of exam format and assessment?
transcript_excerpt: SQE2 has 16 exams total: 12 written exams and 4 oral exams. The 12 written exams include legal drafting, legal research, case or matter analysis and legal writing, taking place on three consecutive days. The 4 oral exams are advocacy and client interview and attendance note, taking place on two consecutive days. Unlike SQE1 which requires passing each individual exam with a scaled score, SQE2 is 50% legal knowledge and 50% skills.

question: What is the exam day schedule and time allocation for SQE1 FLK exams?
transcript_excerpt: Each FLK exam (FLK1 and FLK2) consists of 90 questions split into two sessions: the first 90 questions take two hours and 33 minutes, followed by a 60-minute break where you can leave the test center and access personal belongings, then another 90 questions for another two hours and 33 minutes. The exams take place at Pearson VUE test centres over a two-week window.

episode_title: SQE1 And SQE2 Explained: Everything I Wish I Knew Before!
question: What are the key revision strategies that helped pass SQE1 according to successful candidates?
transcript_excerpt: Effective strategies include starting revision of practice subjects from week one, thoroughly preparing for all classes and assigned reading, making flashcards after each session on platforms like Quizlet, keeping a list of challenging topics to revisit, doing formative and summative exams closed book to mimic the real exam, and starting practice papers two months before the exam even when content is not fully covered. Starting to revise underlying law subjects early (before September if possible) is crucial to avoid feeling overwhelmed in later months.

episode_title: SQE1 And SQE2 Explained: Everything I Wish I Knew Before!
question: What is the recommended approach during the SQE1 exam break between FLK1 and FLK2?
transcript_excerpt: Rather than attempting to revise during the 60-minute break between FLK1 and FLK2, it is better to use that time to genuinely recharge: drink sufficient water, eat filling food with carbohydrates for energy, and avoid reviewing notes. This is because you cannot change answers to questions already completed and reviewing during the break tends to increase anxiety rather than improve performance on the second half of the exam.
